question: A kidney transplant recipient develops a rapid decline in graft function within minutes of completing vascular anastomosis. The excised graft shows widespread fibrin thrombi in glomerular capillaries. What is the mechanism of this rejection?

answers.text: Hyperacute rejection mediated by pre-formed anti-donor HLA antibodies

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Hyperacute rejection occurs within minutes to hours when the recipient has pre-formed antibodies against donor HLA antigens (from prior transplants, blood transfusions, or pregnancies). These antibodies bind graft endothelium, activate complement, trigger platelet aggregation, and cause widespread intravascular thrombosis. The graft becomes cyanotic and must be removed. Pre-transplant crossmatching is performed specifically to prevent this.

answers.text: Acute cellular rejection mediated by host CD8+ cytotoxic T cells

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Acute cellular rejection is T-cell mediated — CD4+ and CD8+ T cells infiltrate the graft parenchyma and cause tubulitis and vasculitis. It occurs days to weeks after transplantation, not within minutes. The immediate onset and thrombotic pattern here indicate pre-formed antibody-mediated hyperacute rejection.

answers.text: Chronic rejection mediated by the indirect allorecognition pathway

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Chronic rejection develops over months to years via the indirect pathway (host T cells recognise processed donor peptides presented on host MHC), causing progressive vascular intimal fibrosis and gradual graft loss. The acute onset within minutes of anastomosis with fibrin thrombi indicates hyperacute rejection by pre-formed anti-donor antibodies.

answers.text: Graft-versus-host disease mediated by donor T lymphocytes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. GVHD occurs when immunocompetent donor T cells attack the immunosuppressed recipient's tissues — characteristically seen in bone marrow transplants, not solid organ transplants. The immediate thrombotic graft failure here is hyperacute rejection caused by pre-formed recipient antibodies against donor HLA antigens.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the three rejection types by timing and mechanism: hyperacute (minutes, pre-formed antibodies, thrombosis), acute (days–weeks, T cells, tubulitis), chronic (months–years, indirect pathway, intimal fibrosis).
Excellent! Hyperacute rejection is the most dramatic form — preventable by pre-transplant crossmatching to detect pre-formed anti-donor antibodies.
